rules.name: Questionnaire flow overview
rules.statement: The employee answers the questionnaire in English in these steps and this order. Each piece of information is asked once and reused for every receiving party; a question appears only when at least one party needs it for this person. Swiss residents with Swiss citizenship or a C permit never see source tax questions.

table.then: First name, last name, date of birth - always.
First working day (contractual start date) - always.
Street, house number (or 'no house number'), postcode, town, country, as on the first working day - always; canton only if living in Switzerland.
Only if living in Switzerland: nationality; if not Swiss, whether they hold a C permit.

Civil status - always. Spouse's/partner's date of birth if Married, Registered partnership or Separated. Spouse's nationality, C permit and country of residence only if needed for the spouse exemption (employee in Switzerland, non-Swiss, no C permit, married or registered partnership).
Only if living in Liechtenstein: daily return; if not, more than 45 non-return days. If the answers mean in principle no source tax liability, steps 7 to 9 are skipped.
Only if a tariff code is needed: denomination; spouse gainfully employed if married or registered partnership.

Only if a tariff code is needed: has children; if yes, one block per child (age status, same household, then custody, common household, shared custody / parental care, alternating custody, main contributor, maintenance over 50% as applicable).
Only if living in Germany: daily return; if yes, certificate of residence; if no, daily return reasonable and, if reasonable, more than 60 non-return days.
Permit reminder for non-Swiss employees and everyone living abroad; answers that no longer apply are discarded; after submission the questionnaire is read-only.

rules.name: Insurance start date
rules.statement: The pension fund insurance start date is derived from the first working day (the contractual start date): if it is the 1st of a month, insurance starts that day; otherwise on the 1st of the following month. It is always derived again from the latest first working day. Assumption on the contractual start date to be verified by a domain expert.

rules.name: Civil status for the pension fund
rules.statement: The civil status entered at the pension fund is the employee's civil status, except that registered partnership and separated are entered as Married (with the spouse's/partner's date of birth). Assumption to be verified by a domain expert.

rules.name: Canton for the pension fund
rules.statement: The pension fund 'Canton' is the canton of residence for employees living in Switzerland; for employees living abroad it is the canton of the place of work, Zurich. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert.

rules.name: Subject to source tax
rules.statement: An employee living abroad is subject to source tax whatever their nationality. An employee living in Switzerland is subject only if not Swiss (anyone with Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss), without a C permit, and not married or in a registered partnership with a Swiss national or C permit holder who lives in Switzerland. 'Here' in HR's wording means Switzerland. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert.
inputs: Spouse Swiss or C permit holder
rules.expression: address_country != "Switzerland" or (address_country == "Switzerland" and nationality != "Switzerland" and holds_c_permit == "no" and not (civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"] and (spouse_nationality == "Switzerland" or spouse_holds_c_permit == "yes") and spouse_residence_country == "Switzerland"))

rules.name: Liechtenstein: in principle no source tax liability
rules.statement: For an employee living in Liechtenstein who returns daily, or who does not return daily and expects at most 45 non-return days, Lonio records 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement' instead of a tariff code, flagged for HR, and skips the tariff questions. With more than 45 non-return days the normal tariff code is computed with the note 'subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert.

rules.name: Child digit
rules.statement: The child digit of the tariff code is the number of children whose result is 'counts' or 'counts with H'; 0 if the employee has no children. The expression gives each child's contribution (1 or 0), summed over all children. There is no maximum number of children.
rules.expression: if_else(has_children == "yes" and child_result in ["counts", "counts with H"], 1, 0)

rules.name: Base tariff letter
rules.statement: Married employees and registered partners get C if the spouse/partner works or receives replacement income, otherwise B. Single, divorced, separated and widowed employees get H if at least one child counts with H, otherwise A. Tariffs G/Q (replacement income) and special tariffs do not occur. The expression is per child; H applies if any child gives H.
rules.expression: if_else(civil_status in ["Married", "Registered partnership"], if_else(spouse_gainful_employment == "yes", "C", "B"), if_else(child_result == "counts with H", "H", "A"))

rules.name: Cross-border tariff applies
rules.statement: For Germany residents the cross-border tariff applies with daily return and a certificate of residence, or without daily return when daily return is reasonable and no more than 60 non-return days are expected. A certificate answered 'not yet' counts as 'no'. In all other cases the normal tariff applies.
rules.expression: address_country == "Germany" and ((daily_return_germany == "yes" and residence_certificate == "yes") or (daily_return_germany == "no" and daily_return_reasonable == "yes" and non_return_days_60 == "no"))

rules.name: Tariff letter
rules.statement: With the cross-border tariff the base letter is replaced: A by L, B by M, C by N, H by P. Otherwise the base letter is used.
rules.expression: if_else(cross_border_tariff, if_else(base_tariff_letter == "A", "L", if_else(base_tariff_letter == "B", "M", if_else(base_tariff_letter == "C", "N", if_else(base_tariff_letter == "H", "P", null)))), base_tariff_letter)

rules.name: Source tax tariff code
rules.statement: For every employee subject to source tax (and not in principle exempt as a Liechtenstein resident), Lonio computes the full Zurich tariff code: tariff letter, child digit and church-tax suffix written together (e.g. C1Y, L0Y). HR no longer uses the calculator. For Liechtenstein residents with more than 45 non-return days the code carries the note 'subject to the double taxation agreement' and is flagged for HR. It is always derived again from the latest answers. Before go-live a domain expert compares it with the calculator for unexplored paths.

table.then: No tariff code; 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the DTA', flagged for HR
Tariff letter + child digit + church-tax suffix (with DTA note for Liechtenstein residents)

rules.expression: if_else(subject_to_source_tax and not liechtenstein_no_source_tax, [tariff_letter, child_count, church_tax_suffix], null)

rules.name: Permit reminder
rules.statement: At the end of the questionnaire, every non-Swiss employee and every employee living abroad (whatever their nationality, as it is not asked) is reminded to bring their permit on the first working day. HR words the reminder so that a Swiss citizen living abroad can see it does not apply to them. It collects no data.

rules.name: Discard answers that no longer apply
rules.statement: Answers to questions that no longer apply after the employee changes an earlier answer are discarded on submission; until then they may be kept so going back and forth loses no input.

rules.name: Read-only after submission
rules.statement: After submission the questionnaire is read-only for the employee. Later changes (move, marriage, new child, certificate of residence handed in later, corrected nationality, changed first working day) are made by HR (later HR-side spec). feature.title: Employee onboarding questionnaire
feature.goal: A new employee answers one short English questionnaire in Lonio, giving each piece of information once and only when a receiving party needs it. From the answers, HR (Muster AG), Pensionskasse Muster and the Zurich source tax side get everything they need, including a computed insurance start date and source tax tariff code.
feature.context:
Today HR at Muster AG collects onboarding data and re-enters it for each receiving party. Missing data blocks registrations: for example, the pension fund cannot register a married employee without the spouse's date of birth (F-pension_portal-a0065b, F-hr_transcript-2334d8). The first working day often moves, for example when the employee negotiates an earlier exit with the old employer, and the insurance start date depends on it (F-hr_transcript-e3721e, F-hr_transcript-1d5c07). HR posts many documents and needs a complete address (F-hr_transcript-c0fe95). HR also decides who is subject to source tax with its own rule and then clicks through the Zurich tariff calculator by hand (F-hr_transcript-5af8d0, F-hr_transcript-34494f).

Lonio replaces this with one questionnaire. It asks each fact once (G-01) and asks primary facts so it can derive values such as the insurance start date (G-08). It computes the full Zurich tariff code itself (D-001). It does not ask what no party needs, such as AHV data, IT equipment, the permit type or the income type (G-03, D-005, D-006). Only the employee side is in scope: how data is sent to the parties and the HR screens are separate topics (G-04, D-034). Several mappings are assumptions that a domain expert still has to verify (D-002, D-003, D-004, D-039 to D-046). Before go-live, a domain expert must compare the computed tariff code with the calculator (D-009).

sections.title: Questionnaire flow overview
sections.purpose: Define the steps, their order and the conditions for showing each one. Also define the end of the questionnaire: permit reminder, discarding answers that no longer apply, and read-only after submission.

stories.title: Show the source tax step only to employees who are subject to source tax
stories.i_want: the source tax questions (denomination, spouse employment, children, cross-border questions) to be shown only to employees who are subject to source tax
stories.so_that: I no longer have to work out up front who must answer them, and employees who are not subject to source tax are not asked for personal data no party needs
stories.priority_reason: HR states it never knows up front who has to answer the source tax questions; asking everyone would collect data that must not be collected (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Who sees the source tax questions
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has answered country of residence and, where asked, nationality, C permit, civil status and the spouse questions
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire decides whether to show the source tax step
acceptance_criteria.then: the source tax step is shown only if the employee is subject to source tax: everyone living abroad, whatever their nationality; and anyone living in Switzerland who is not Swiss, has no C permit and is not married or in a registered partnership with a Swiss national or C permit holder who lives in Switzerland. Anyone with Swiss citizenship counts as Swiss. Registered partnership counts as married and separated as single. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert: HR's consolidated rule is applied as stated, and 'here' in HR's wording means Switzerland (D-043). The civil status mapping is also an assumption (D-003).

Single non-Swiss resident without C permit
Married to a non-Swiss spouse without C permit
Married to a C permit holder living abroad

acceptance_criteria.title: Spouse questions for source tax only when they can change the outcome
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: the civil status and spouse step is shown
acceptance_criteria.then: the spouse's nationality, C permit and country of residence are asked only if the employee is not Swiss, has no C permit and is married or in a registered partnership; the spouse's C permit only if the spouse is not Swiss; the spouse's country of residence only if the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit. Employees living abroad are never asked these questions, because they are subject to source tax anyway.

stories.title: Ask the steps in an order that avoids unneeded questions
stories.i_want: to answer one short English questionnaire in a fixed order of steps, where each step only appears when it applies to me
stories.so_that: I answer only what a receiving party needs from me and every later step can depend on what I already said
stories.priority_reason: The order is what makes conditional questions possible; without it the questionnaire either blocks registrations or over-collects personal data (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Steps and order
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee opens the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they go through it
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire is in English and has these steps in this order: 1 Personal details (first name, last name, date of birth - always); 2 Start (first working day, the contractual start date even on a weekend or public holiday - always); 3 Home address as on the first working day (street, house number or 'no house number', postcode, town, country - always; canton only if living in Switzerland); 4 Nationality and permit (only if living in Switzerland: nationality, and whether they hold a C permit if not Swiss); 5 Civil status and spouse; 6 Liechtenstein cross-border (only if living in Liechtenstein); 7 Source tax personal details (denomination; spouse employment if married or in a registered partnership); 8 Children; 9 Germany cross-border (only if living in Germany); 10 Summary and submission. Steps 7 to 9 appear only when a tariff code is needed. Assumptions, to be verified by a domain expert: the first working day is the contractual start date (D-039); address and country are those on the first working day (D-041); the house number is required, with a 'no house number' option (D-042); employees living abroad are not asked for the canton, Zurich is entered for them (D-002); there is no maximum number of children and a child's age is judged on the first working day (D-044).

acceptance_criteria.title: Liechtenstein cross-border questions come first and can skip the tariff questions
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the source tax part of the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: they are first asked whether they expect to return daily to their main residence in Liechtenstein and, if not, whether they expect more than 45 work-related non-return days in the calendar year; this comes before denomination, spouse employment and children. With daily return or at most 45 non-return days the result is 'in principle no source tax liability, subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR, and denomination, spouse employment and children are not asked. With more than 45 non-return days these questions are asked and the normal tariff code is recorded with the note 'subject to the double taxation agreement', flagged for HR. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert (D-040). How HR sees the flag belongs to the later HR-side spec (see OQ-hr-side-follow-ups).

stories.title: Ask each piece of information once and reuse it for every receiving party
stories.i_want: each piece of information to be asked from the employee only once and recorded for every party that needs it (HR, Pensionskasse Muster, source tax)
stories.so_that: I no longer re-enter the same data for each party and registrations are not blocked by missing data such as the spouse's date of birth
stories.priority_reason: Missing data blocks registrations today (the fund cannot register a married employee without the spouse's date of birth) and asking once is the core goal of the feature (G-01).

acceptance_criteria.title: Shared answers are asked once
acceptance_criteria.given: an answer is needed by more than one party, such as civil status (pension fund and source tax) or country of residence (HR, pension fund and source tax)
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee goes through the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: the question appears exactly once and its answer is recorded for HR for every party that needs it; how the data reaches each party is a separate topic and not part of this questionnaire

examples.name: Civil status used by fund and source tax

acceptance_criteria.title: A question is asked only when a party needs it for this person
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee's earlier answers show that no party needs a piece of information for them
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire reaches that question
acceptance_criteria.then: the question is not asked. For example, the spouse's or partner's date of birth is asked from married, registered-partnership and separated employees, not from divorced or widowed ones. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert: registered partnership and separated are entered at the fund as Married, which requires the spouse's date of birth (D-003, D-004). Nothing outside the needs of HR, the pension fund and source tax is asked (no AHV data, IT equipment, permit type or income type).

stories.title: Remind non-Swiss employees and employees living abroad to bring their permit
stories.i_want: the questionnaire to end with a reminder to bring the permit on the first working day for every non-Swiss employee and every employee living abroad
stories.so_that: fewer new employees forget their permit on their first day
stories.priority_reason: Explicit HR wish ('half of them forget'); it removes a recurring nuisance but blocks no registration.

acceptance_criteria.title: Who gets the permit reminder
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has reached the summary step
acceptance_criteria.when: the summary is shown
acceptance_criteria.then: a reminder to bring their permit on the first working day is shown to every employee living in Switzerland who is not Swiss and to every employee living abroad, whatever their nationality (nationality is not asked of them). A Swiss citizen living in Switzerland gets no reminder. The reminder collects no data. HR words it so that a Swiss citizen living abroad can see it does not apply to them; this spec states only its purpose.

acceptance_criteria.title: Answers that no longer apply are discarded on submission

acceptance_criteria.then: the answer to that question is discarded and not recorded for any party; only answers to questions that apply to the final answers are recorded

stories.title: Make the questionnaire read-only after submission and derive results from the latest answers
stories.i_want: the questionnaire to be read-only for the employee once submitted, with later changes made by HR and every derived result always computed again from the latest answers
stories.so_that: the recorded data stays consistent and the insurance start date, civil status for the fund and for source tax, source tax liability and tariff code always match the current facts, for example when the first working day moves
stories.priority_reason: The first working day often moves and the insurance start date depends on it; stale derived values would give wrong registrations, but HR handles the changes.

acceptance_criteria.title: Employee cannot change answers after submission
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they open it again
acceptance_criteria.then: they can see their answers but cannot change them; any later change (a move, a marriage, a new child, a certificate of residence handed in later, a corrected nationality, a new first working day) is made by HR. acceptance_criteria.title: Derived results follow the latest answers
acceptance_criteria.given: an answer has been changed after submission
acceptance_criteria.when: the derived results are looked at
acceptance_criteria.then: the insurance start date, the civil status for the pension fund and for source tax, whether the employee is subject to source tax and the tariff code are derived again from the latest answers; for the first working day the latest date always counts and no history of earlier dates is kept. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert: the insurance start date is derived only from the first working day, which is the contractual start date (D-039).

sections.title: Personal details and home address
sections.purpose: Collect the employee's name, date of birth and complete home address as it applies on the first working day, plus the canton for the pension fund.

stories.title: Collect the employee's name and date of birth
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their first name, last name and date of birth in the onboarding questionnaire
stories.so_that: the occupational pension registration can be submitted. The fund's form rejects a registration where any of these required fields is empty. HR also needs the name to identify the employee and to address the documents it posts to them.
stories.priority_reason: First name, last name and date of birth are required fields in the pension fund registration. If one is missing, the registration is blocked (F-pension_portal-44a27b).

acceptance_criteria.title: Name is asked of every employee and cannot be left empty
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire, whatever their country of residence, nationality or civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the personal details
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their first name and their last name. Both answers are required, so the questionnaire cannot be submitted while either is empty. The answers are recorded for the pension fund registration (fields 'First name' and 'Last name') and for HR, which uses them to identify the employee and address the documents it posts.

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth is asked of every employee as a day, month and year
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the personal details
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for their date of birth as day, month and year (DD.MM.YYYY, e.g. 14.03.1990). The answer is required, so the questionnaire cannot be submitted without it. It is recorded for the pension fund registration (field 'Date of birth').

stories.title: Collect a complete postal home address
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their complete home address (street, house number, postcode, town and country) as it applies on their first working day
stories.so_that: HR can post the many documents it sends to employees to an address that is complete and correct from the start of employment
stories.priority_reason: HR posts many documents to employees and states that the address 'has to be complete' (F-hr_transcript-3beee8, F-hr_transcript-c0fe95). An incomplete address means documents cannot be delivered.

acceptance_criteria.title: The full postal address is asked of every employee
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the home address
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked for street, house number, postcode, town and country, written as a normal postal address on an envelope and nothing more. Street, postcode, town and country are required. The address is recorded for HR so it can post documents.

acceptance_criteria.title: House number is required, with an explicit 'no house number' answer
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee enters their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the address has a house number, or the address has none
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee must either enter the house number or state explicitly 'no house number'. The house number cannot simply be left blank. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert: HR wants a complete address including the house number, and some addresses have none (D-042).

acceptance_criteria.title: The address asked is the one that applies on the first working day
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee who is moving around the time they start, e.g. relocating to Switzerland for the new job
acceptance_criteria.when: they enter their home address
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire makes clear that the address to give is the one where they will live on their first working day, not an earlier one. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert (D-041).

stories.title: Use the home address country as the country of residence
stories.i_want: the country of the employee's home address to be used as their country of residence, without asking for it a second time
stories.so_that: Lonio can tell whether the employee lives abroad (and is therefore subject to source tax whatever their nationality) and which follow-up questions apply, while the employee states the country only once
stories.priority_reason: Country of residence decides who is subject to source tax and which further questions are asked. HR today does not know up front who has to answer the source tax questions (F-hr_transcript-b84498, F-hr_transcript-5af8d0).

acceptance_criteria.title: Country is given once and named in English
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee enters their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: they give the country
acceptance_criteria.then: they choose the country by its English name (e.g. Switzerland, Germany, Liechtenstein). This one answer counts as their country of residence on the first working day. The employee is not asked about their country of residence anywhere else in the questionnaire. The answer is recorded for HR (postal address), for source tax (residence) and for the pension fund (to decide the canton). The residence-on-the-first-working-day reading is an assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-041).

acceptance_criteria.title: Living abroad means subject to source tax and no nationality question
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee whose home address is outside Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: they continue the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio treats them as subject to source tax whatever their nationality, as in HR's rule where 'here' means Switzerland. They are not asked for their nationality or for a canton. An employee whose home address is in Switzerland is asked for their nationality and canton, and their source tax liability depends on those further answers. Applying HR's rule as stated is an assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-043).

stories.title: Ask Swiss residents for their canton
stories.i_want: every registration to carry a canton: the canton of residence for employees living in Switzerland and Zurich, the canton of the place of work, for employees living abroad
stories.so_that: the required 'Canton' field of the registration is never empty, and employees living abroad are not asked a question the fund's canton list cannot answer for them
stories.priority_reason: 'Canton' is a required field. Without it the pension fund registration is blocked (F-pension_portal-44a27b, F-pension_portal-6c621f).

acceptance_criteria.title: Only employees living in Switzerland choose their canton
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee has given the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the country is Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: they are asked to choose their canton of residence. The answer is required. The choice is one of the 26 cantons on the pension fund's list: Aargau, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Basel-Landschaft, Basel-Stadt, Bern, Fribourg, Geneva, Glarus, Graubünden, Jura, Lucerne, Neuchâtel, Nidwalden, Obwalden, Schaffhausen, Schwyz, Solothurn, St. Gallen, Thurgau, Ticino, Uri, Valais, Vaud, Zug, Zurich. If the country is anything other than Switzerland, the canton is not asked. Assumption, to be verified by a domain expert (D-002).

acceptance_criteria.title: Canton recorded for the pension fund
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee has submitted the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio determines the canton for the pension fund registration
acceptance_criteria.then: for an employee living in Switzerland, it is the canton they chose. For an employee living in any other country, it is Zurich, the canton of Muster AG's place of work, which Lonio enters without asking. Because the fund's list has no option for a residence outside Switzerland and the fund does not say whether 'Canton' means residence or work, this mapping is an assumption to be verified by a domain expert (D-002). The canton is derived again from the latest answers whenever they change.

sections.title: Civil status and spouse data
sections.purpose: Ask for civil status and, where the fund requires it, the spouse's or registered partner's date of birth. Map civil status to the pension fund's list and to the source tax groups.

stories.title: Ask every employee for their civil status
stories.i_want: every new employee to state their civil status, choosing from Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, Registered partnership or Separated
stories.so_that: the required 'Civil status' field of the registration can be filled and source tax can tell the married path from the single path, without HR having to ask the employee again
stories.priority_reason: Civil status is a required field of the pension fund registration, and the source tax tariff code depends on it. Without it, both the registration and the tariff code are blocked.

acceptance_criteria.title: Civil status is always asked and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire, whatever their residence, nationality or source tax situation
acceptance_criteria.when: they reach the civil status question
acceptance_criteria.then: the question is asked, and the employee cannot submit the questionnaire without answering it

acceptance_criteria.title: Exactly six civil status options
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee is asked for their civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: they choose an answer
acceptance_criteria.then: they can choose exactly one of: Single, Married, Divorced, Widowed, Registered partnership, Separated. The first four are the pension fund's own list, written as the fund writes them. Registered partnership and Separated are added so that the calculator's groups can be answered and employees such as Daniel, who is in a registered partnership, can answer truthfully. Assumption to be verified by a domain expert: offering these two extra options and mapping them as described in the stories on civil status for the pension fund and for source tax.

acceptance_criteria.title: Who receives the civil status

stories.so_that: I know whether a Swiss resident can be subject to source tax without collecting nationality or permit data that no party needs

acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks for the employee's nationality and an answer is required. Anyone who holds Swiss citizenship answers Switzerland, even if they also hold another nationality (decision D-008, an assumption to be verified by a domain expert). When the country is any other country, nationality is not asked, because an employee living abroad is subject to source tax whatever their nationality.

acceptance_criteria.then: Lonio asks whether the employee holds a C permit (permanent residence), with the answers yes or no, and an answer is required. No other permit type is asked. When the nationality is Switzerland, the C permit question is not asked.

Employees living abroad are not asked their nationality; they get the permit reminder whatever their nationality (decision D-038).

It is not asked for Single, Divorced, Widowed or Separated (separated counts as single for source tax, decision D-003, an assumption to be verified by a domain expert), and not asked of Swiss employees, C permit holders or employees living abroad. That the spouse questions are needed only when the employee would otherwise be subject is an inference from HR's rule.

stories.i_want: Lonio to decide for every employee, from the answers given, whether they are subject to source tax, following HR's consolidated rule

Registered partnership counts as married (decision D-003, an assumption to be verified by a domain expert).

acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio derives the tariff code
acceptance_criteria.then: the tariff letter is H and the child digit still counts every counted child (for example one child that counts and one that counts with H give H2). flow.intro: The questionnaire has 8 steps, in English. Only applicable questions are shown, and a step where no question applies to the employee is skipped. The order follows dependencies: identity and address first, because residence decides what is asked next. Nationality and civil status follow, because they decide whether source tax applies. Cross-border questions come before denomination, spouse and children, because for Liechtenstein residents they can make the tariff questions unnecessary. Each piece of information is asked once and reused for every receiving party. Swiss residents with Swiss citizenship or a C permit never see the source tax steps.

steps.title: About you
steps.asks: First name, last name, date of birth and the first working day.

steps.title: Home address
steps.asks: Street, house number, postcode, town and country of the home address that applies on the first working day; the canton of residence only if the country is Switzerland.

steps.title: Nationality and C permit
steps.asks: Nationality; whether the employee holds a C permit only if not Swiss.

steps.title: Civil status and spouse
steps.asks: Civil status; the spouse's or registered partner's date of birth if Married, Registered partnership or Separated; the spouse's nationality only if the employee is not Swiss, has no C permit and is married or in a registered partnership; whether the spouse holds a C permit if the spouse is not Swiss; the spouse's country of residence if the spouse is Swiss or holds a C permit.
steps.shown_to: Everyone (spouse questions only where their conditions apply)

steps.title: Cross-border commuting
steps.asks: For Liechtenstein residents: daily return, then, if not daily, whether more than 45 non-return days are expected. For Germany residents: daily return; certificate of residence if daily return ("not yet" is allowed); if not daily, whether daily return is reasonable (under 100 km) and, if reasonable but not done, whether more than 60 non-return days are expected.
steps.shown_to: Employees subject to source tax who live in Germany or Liechtenstein

steps.title: Source tax details
steps.asks: Denomination; whether the spouse or partner is gainfully employed (only if married or in a registered partnership); whether the employee has children.
steps.shown_to: Employees subject to source tax who need a tariff code (Liechtenstein residents only with more than 45 non-return days)

steps.title: Children
steps.asks: For each child: minor or adult in first education; whether the child lives in the same household; then, depending on the answers, custody, common household with the other parent, shared custody, parental care, alternating custody, main financial contributor and whether more than 50% of maintenance is provided.

flow.closing: After the last step the employee submits the questionnaire.
